claims.claim: WolfeWiki prints the Fifth Head dedication as 'To Damon Knight, who one well-remembered June evening in 1966 grew me from a bean.'

claims.quote: who one well-remembered June evening in 1966 grew me from a bean

verdicts.trueWording: who one night in 1966 grew me from a bean
verdicts.note: Live gwern HTML fetched raw (SFS #46, Nov 1988 masthead). McCaffery's question prints the dedication in that wording; the second limb was cross-checked on the WolfeWiki Trip,Trap page fetched for index 668, which prints the 'well-remembered June evening' wording. Both printings confirmed on raw pages.

verdicts.trueWording: who one well-remembered June evening in 1966 grew me from a bean
verdicts.note: Live wolfewiki.com page fetched raw; the dedication sentence closes the section headed 'A note about the writing of the story'. Word-for-word match.

verdicts.trueWording: he invited me to write a novel for Berkely
verdicts.note: Live gwern .txt fetched raw. In the answer to Robert's unsolicited-manuscript question Wolfe says Damon Knight, to whom he had sold several short stories, was connected with a publisher (he names Berkley Books) and issued the invitation. All limbs on the page.

verdicts.trueWording: Norbert Slepyan of Scribner's was there at that meeting
verdicts.note: Live gwern HTML fetched raw. In the answer on the structure of Cerberus Wolfe says he presented the title story at Milford, Slepyan was there and liked it, and would publish a book if Wolfe wrote two other stories of roughly the same length. Every limb supported.

verdicts.trueWording: Plant Engineering Magazine, Barrington, IL, senior editor, 1972-84
verdicts.note: Live gwern .txt fetched raw; the CAREER line of the Gale entry (Major 21st-Century Writers, ed. Matthews, vol. 5, 2005) carries the quotation word for word, so the dating limb is verified. The comparison limb is not on this page. Checked separately: Ultan's Library (ultan.org.uk/plant-engineering/, fetched raw) does give 1972-1984 and quotes Wolfe calling himself a senior editor, so that half holds; the Plant Engineering obituary could not be located (two candidate URLs 404, Wayback CDX returned nothing), so the 'against the magazine's own obituary' half is unverified here.
verdicts.unsupportedLimb: that Gale thereby agrees with Ultan's Library against Plant Engineering's own obituary

verdicts.trueWording: David was Gene's editor for The Book of the New Sun
verdicts.note: Live reactormag page fetched raw: byline Theresa DeLucci, published March 13, 2017 (the former Tor.com URL). The sentence stands alone as a one-line paragraph in the World Horror Con 2002 passage, and the same passage establishes she was his Tor Books co-worker.

verdicts.trueWording: usually suggested how to change the story to make it acceptable
verdicts.note: Live Archives West finding aid fetched raw (credit line 'Joyce Griffith and Stephanie Kays 2015'). The Content Description sentence about Knight's letters of rejection continues 'and/or where it might be submitted for more likely acceptance', covering the second limb.

verdicts.trueWording: Among them: Gene Wolfe, Vonda McIntyre, Gardner Dozois
verdicts.note: Live Archives West finding aid fetched raw. Content Description says there are many letters in the Orbit correspondence containing material of personal interest, then lists Wolfe first among nine names. The page attributes 'many' to the Orbit correspondence as a whole, not to Wolfe individually; it establishes that Wolfe letters are among them, not their number.
verdicts.unsupportedLimb: that the correspondence holds many letters specifically from Gene Wolfe

verdicts.trueWording: 'literary' SF (by Le Guin, Aldiss, Wolfe, and others)
verdicts.note: Live markrkelly.com post fetched raw (posted Thursday 22 March 2018 by Mark R. Kelly, Views from Crestmont Drive). The paragraph on the last chapter says the book ends with a 1966 coda attempting prediction of how the field would split into divisions, the parenthesis quoted being the literary one. All limbs supported.

verdicts.trueWording: our field's most consequential editor since John W. Campbell
verdicts.note: Live Making Light post fetched raw, 'David Geddes Hartwell, 1941-2016', posted by Patrick Nielsen Hayden, January 19 2016. The sentence closes the penultimate paragraph of the post body. Word-for-word match.

verdicts.trueWording: My other sales were stories that Damon Knight had turned down
verdicts.note: Locus #500 PDF fetched from gwern and text-extracted with pdftotext -raw. The preceding sentences describe sending 'Trip-Trap' to Orbit and Knight buying it, then 'For years after that, the Orbit series was my main market.' Both limbs on the page; the OCR runs some word pairs together.

verdicts.trueWording: only for published writers - either people he was publishing in Orbit
verdicts.note: Same Locus #500 PDF, extracted text. Wolfe's answer about Milford continues 'or people he would like to publish in Orbit', matching the claim exactly.

verdicts.trueWording: an editor from Scribners came up to me and said
verdicts.note: Same Locus #500 PDF. The 2002 telling names no editor: a case-insensitive search for 'Slepyan' over the whole extracted PDF returns nothing, and only 'an editor from Scribners' appears. The 1988 naming limb was cross-checked on the McCaffery page fetched for index 672.

verdicts.trueWording: senior editor of Plant Engineering from 1972 - 84
verdicts.note: Same Locus #500 PDF. The biographical sidebar beside the Gaiman conversation reads that way (OCR joins words as 'editor ofPlant Engineeringfrom 1972 - 84'); the preceding clause supplies 'senior'.

verdicts.trueWording: You know, I think the rewrite has really improved this
verdicts.note: Same Locus #500 PDF: Wolfe's 2002 quotation of Pohl runs on 'I'm glad you let me see it again' (OCR 'youlet'). The 1988 wording limb was cross-checked on the McCaffery page, which prints Pohl's letter with the glad-clause first and 'The re write has really improved it.' Both limbs verified on raw pages.
